blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In practice, direct and indirect taxes need very different processes. Direct taxes — income tax and corporate tax — are calculated from results and filed periodically. The work is analytical: you read the accounts, apply the rules, file the return, and pay the bill.

Indirect taxes — VAT above all — are an operational flow that never stops. Every invoice carries VAT in; every purchase carries VAT out. The company lives inside a continuous cycle of collection, reconciliation, and settlement with the tax office.

A finance team that treats both taxes with the same process quietly gets into trouble. Direct taxes need sharp analytical attention a few times a year. Indirect taxes need steady, repetitive discipline every single week. Mixing the rhythms — treating VAT as an analytical exercise, or treating corporate tax as a routine task — leads to errors in both.

items.q: According to the text, how are direct taxes calculated?
items.why: "Direct taxes… are calculated from results and filed periodically."

items.q: What best describes indirect taxes such as VAT?
options: A one-off calculation at year end
An operational flow that never stops
An analytical exercise done once a year
A rule that only applies to purchases
items.why: "Indirect taxes — VAT above all — are an operational flow that never stops."

items.q: The text suggests that a team using the SAME process for both taxes will…
items.why: Inferência: "A finance team that treats both taxes with the same process quietly gets into trouble."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: VAT should be handled as a steady weekly routine.
Both taxes can safely share one identical workflow.
The two taxes follow different rhythms.
Corporate tax deserves sharp analytical attention.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta contra tratar os dois impostos com o mesmo processo.

items.q: What does "leads to errors in both" at the end imply?
options: Errors happen only during the annual filing
Only VAT suffers when the rhythms are mixed
The tax office causes most of the errors
Mixing the rhythms damages direct AND indirect tax work
items.why: Inferência: misturar os ritmos não prejudica só um imposto — os dois saem errados.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry organizando o fluxo de trabalho da equipe financeira. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me explain how I want us to split the work from now on. For months we handled direct tax and VAT in the same meeting, and honestly, it created a lot of confusion. So we are going to run two separate tracks.

Track one is the analytical one. Corporate tax, income tax — these come from the accounts, and we only touch them a few times a year. When we do, I want full focus: read the numbers, apply the rules, file cleanly. No distractions.

Track two is VAT, and this one never sleeps. Every invoice, every purchase, every week. It is not clever work, but it is relentless. Collection, reconciliation, settlement — the same steady cycle, over and over. If we skip a week, the mess grows fast.

The mistake we kept making was mixing the rhythms. We treated VAT like a puzzle to solve once, and we treated corporate tax like a routine chore. Both went wrong. So from Monday, VAT gets its own weekly slot, and direct tax gets its quiet analytical block. Two rhythms, one team.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is Harry splitting the work into two tracks?
options: The team was too small for one meeting
He wants to reduce the headcount
Handling both taxes together created confusion
The tax office asked him to
items.why: "we handled direct tax and VAT in the same meeting, and… it created a lot of confusion."

items.q: How often does Harry say the analytical track is touched?
options: Only a few times a year
items.why: "these come from the accounts, and we only touch them a few times a year."

items.q: How does Harry describe the VAT track?
options: Relentless, steady work that never sleeps
Clever work done once a year
items.why: "this one never sleeps… It is not clever work, but it is relentless."

items.q: What does Harry mean by "if we skip a week, the mess grows fast"?
options: The team should skip a week to rest
The tax office fines the company weekly
VAT problems pile up quickly when the routine is dropped
items.why: Inferência: o fluxo de VAT é contínuo — pular uma semana acumula erros rapidamente.

items.q: What can we infer about Harry's view of the past approach?
options: He blames the tax office for the confusion
He thinks it worked well and only needs minor tweaks
He sees mixing the rhythms as the root of the problem
He believes both taxes should stay in one meeting
items.why: Inferência: "The mistake we kept making was mixing the rhythms" — ele aponta a mistura como a causa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Corporate tax is filed periodically, not every day." Periodically means…
items.why: Periodically = periodicamente, em intervalos regulares e espaçados.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "VAT is an ___ flow — invoices and purchases arrive every single day."
items.why: Operational flow = fluxo operacional, o trabalho contínuo de todo dia (VAT).

items.q: "Before we pay the tax office, we do a full reconciliation." A reconciliation is…
options: a request to delay the payment
a forecast of next year's tax
a public announcement of the figures
a check that matches records so the numbers agree
items.why: Reconciliation = conciliação: conferir e casar os registros para que os números batam.

items.q: "The VAT cycle ends with the monthly settlement to the tax office." Settlement here means…
options: the final payment that clears the balance
items.why: Settlement = liquidação: o acerto/pagamento final que zera o saldo com o fisco.

items.q: "Direct taxes need sharp attention a few times a year." Sharp attention means…
options: attention shared with many other tasks
items.why: Sharp attention = atenção aguçada: foco preciso e concentrado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de finanças e impostos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the VAT return before we file it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new weekly VAT routine across all branches." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two analysts pushed back on the new schedule." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado (aqui, não levaram).

items.q: "If we fall behind on the VAT reconciliation, the errors pile up." To fall behind on means to…
options: delegate the work to a junior
fail to keep up with the work on time
items.why: Fall behind on = ficar atrasado, não conseguir acompanhar o ritmo do trabalho.
